problem: Turn on the "YouTube Analytics API" in your Google Cloud project, then tap Analyze now again.
summary: Among the nine films at least two days old, the two leaders show a familiar kitchen object doing something viewers can see and test. The bottom two cover car-roof frost and the Leonid meteor shower, so familiarity and surprise alone don’t explain the gap. These are early signs from two films per quarter, and the view counts can’t establish what caused the difference.

working.lesson: Build the explanation around a visible result with a familiar object.
working.evidence: The top quarter of the nine films at least two days old, rounded to two films, was the spoon swinging toward tap water at 593.7 views per day and the raw-versus-boiled egg spin test at 488.4. The hotter-pan water demo also reached 607.4 vi…

working.lesson: A direct claim about a visible surprise is a hook worth testing.
working.evidence: The hotter-pan film has the highest current rate at 607.4 views per day and opens with the claim that water lasts longer on a hotter pan. The first sentences are missing for both mature leaders. The topic notes describe their opening scene…

working.lesson: The two mature leaders also drew more likes per view than the bottom two.
working.evidence: Together the spoon and egg films earned 46 likes on 2,673 views, about 1.7%, and zero comments. The frost and Leonid films earned 9 likes on 1,024 views, about 0.9%, and one comment. These counts measure reactions and give no evidence abou…

notWorking.lesson: The seasonal sky event and the weather puzzle had the lowest mature view rates.
notWorking.evidence: The Leonid meteor shower had 89.9 views per day and car-roof frost had 173.3. The seasons misconception film reached 467.8, so the weak Leonid result gives little reason to cut astronomy as a whole. The frost film already opens on the visu…

notWorking.lesson: Runtime has no clear winner yet.
notWorking.evidence: The mature leaders ran 34 and 38 seconds, and the bottom two ran 26 and 27 seconds. The 25-second impulse film reached 422.5 views per day, while the 42-second seasons film reached 467.8.

notWorking.lesson: Language, voice, real photos, animation, and AI media offer no dependable rule from this batch.
notWorking.evidence: Both mature leaders were labeled en, as was the low-ranking frost film. The low-ranking Leonid film was labeled en-US. Voice was unrecorded for all 13 films. Both mature quarters used real photos and had AI media marked false. The only fil…

notWorking.lesson: Hashtag count and the shared science tag offer no basis for choosing a tag strategy.
notWorking.evidence: All 13 films used eight hashtags and included #science. Both mature leaders used kitchen tags, which overlap with the subject of each film.

notWorking.lesson: There’s no repeatable posting day or hour yet.
notWorking.evidence: The mature leaders posted Thursday at 09:00 and 14:00. The bottom two posted Wednesday at 09:00 and Tuesday at 10:00. The two mature 09:00 uploads reached 593.7 and 173.3 views per day, and every Friday upload was under two days old.

rules: Put a familiar object and its surprising behavior in the first shot.
Use the first sentence to say what the viewer is about to see in plain English.
Show two conditions side by side when the difference is the point.
Show the result before naming the effect, then animate the mechanism.
moreTopics: Everyday kitchen objects that move in unexpected ways
Side-by-side kitchen tests with a visible way to tell two things apart
lessTopics: Date-led sky events like the Leonid meteor shower, pending another test
hooks: Water lasts longer on a hotter pan.
experiments: Across comparable demos, alternate a plain surprise statement with a prediction question. Compare views per day at the same age and record early and end retention if it becomes available.
Try 25–28 seconds and 34–38 seconds on similar demos while keeping the opening and visual approach comparable.
Rotate similar demos through Thursday 09:00 and Thursday 14:00 over several weeks, then compare views per day at the same age.
